title: ReSMiPS: A ReRAM-based Sparse Mixed-precision Solver with Fast Matrix Reordering Algorithm
problem: Sparse matrix equation solvers on digital platforms suffer from memory bandwidth bottlenecks in large-scale storage and computation; ReRAM-based CIM offers promise but struggles to achieve high precision and energy efficiency simultaneously.
motivation: Sparse matrix solutions are essential for scientific computing but face fundamental memory access challenges; ReRAM CIM enables in-memory analog computation but requires innovation to maintain numerical precision while achieving energy gains.
method: ReSMiPS combines a novel Fast Sparse Matrix Reordering (FSMR) algorithm with an In-memory float64 (IF64) data format implemented in analog ReRAM arrays, coupled with a hybrid-domain solution framework that performs floating-point sparse matrix operations directly in the ReRAM array.
key_novelty: In-memory float64 analog computation in ReRAM arrays enabling direct sparse matrix solving with BiCGSTAB-level precision (< 10^-15 error) at 100× better speed/energy than CPU/GPU.
contributions: Fast Sparse Matrix Reordering algorithm optimizing data placement for ReRAM computation
In-memory float64 (IF64) data format enabling high-precision floating-point in analog ReRAM
Hybrid-domain solution framework achieving 100× speed and energy improvement over CPU/GPU while maintaining numerical precision
limitations: Scalability to very large problem sizes and applicability to unstructured sparse patterns not discussed.
primary_theme: ReRAM-based in-memory analog sparse matrix solver
